data.name: Watch Me Jump
data.detailed_description:
Watch Me Jump is a digital story of scandal and betrayal, played out in four quarters. As WNBA all-star Audra Bee Mills, the player will have to navigate through the dialogue, shaping Audra's personality along the way through the choices made.


Watch Me Jump is the first video game from award-winning playwright Jeremy Gable, and is adapted from his play of the same name. The player takes the role of Audra Bee Mills, who is about to become the highest paid women’s basketball player in the world. But on the night before playoffs, a scandal threatens to overturn everything she has worked for. And Audra has to figure out how to get through the night without losing either her dignity or her career.


As the player moves through the game, various choices will influence Audra’s experience and personality. And with the decisions made, the player will help Audra determine what it truly means to be “the best".


Featuring completely original artwork and music, Watch Me Jump is a throwback to the games of the 8-bit era, combining the look and feel of old-school RPGs and text based adventures with a unique and original 21st century story. And simple, easy-to-use controls help move the player through the many twists of this intense and humorous journey.

data.short_description: An entirely different kind of basketball game. A narrative-driven journey told in four quarters.

reviews.review:
Watch Me Jump takes the familiar world of professional basketball and uses it for something considerably different from a conventional sports game. Instead of asking players to master shooting, passing, defense, or team management, it concentrates on conversations, personal decisions, ambition, and the consequences of pursuing success. The game was developed and published by Jeremy Gable, who adapted the concept from his own stage play. That theatrical origin strongly influences the finished experience, making this primarily an interactive drama rather than a basketball simulation.

The story centers on Audra Bee Mills, a successful professional basketball player standing on the edge of an enormous career milestone. She is about to become the highest-paid player in women's basketball, but the situation changes dramatically when a scandal emerges immediately before the playoffs. What should have been a moment of celebration becomes a stressful confrontation with the people in her life, forcing Audra to consider how much she is prepared to sacrifice to protect her career and reputation.

Rather than presenting players with elaborate action sequences, Watch Me Jump builds its gameplay around dialogue and decision-making. Conversations allow the player to influence Audra's behavior, personality, and relationships. Choices can make her appear sympathetic, aggressive, calculating, vulnerable, or determined depending on how situations are handled. The interesting part is that decisions are not always framed around an obvious correct response. The game frequently places personal interests against professional ambitions, encouraging the player to consider what success actually means to Audra.

One of the more creative elements is the way the narrative is divided into four quarters. It borrows terminology from basketball while essentially structuring the experience like a theatrical production. This is an effective connection between the sporting setting and the game's storytelling ambitions. Basketball remains important to the circumstances surrounding the characters, but the emotional conflicts occurring away from the court receive most of the attention.

The presentation reinforces the game's independent personality through retro-inspired visuals reminiscent of older role-playing and adventure games. The simple pixel-based appearance might initially suggest a lighthearted experience, yet the narrative explores considerably heavier material. Original artwork and music help establish an atmosphere that feels deliberately minimal rather than simply technologically limited. The visual style leaves plenty of room for the dialogue and characters to remain the focus.

Its stage-play origins can occasionally make the experience feel more like reading and directing a dramatic performance than playing a traditional video game. There is relatively little mechanical complexity outside choosing responses and following the developing story. Players who enjoy visual novels, interactive fiction, or choice-driven adventures may find this approach appealing because there are few distractions from the narrative. Those expecting substantial basketball gameplay, exploration, combat, or complicated systems are likely to find the interaction too restricted.

The story also deals with mature subjects despite its colorful retro appearance. Strong language and alcohol are present, while the narrative addresses an off-screen assault and includes a brief instance of self-inflicted violence. These elements support the more serious dramatic conflicts surrounding Audra and the people around her. Humor provides occasional relief, preventing the experience from becoming entirely bleak while maintaining the sense that the protagonist's career and personal relationships are under significant pressure.

Replay value depends largely on the player's interest in experimenting with different dialogue choices. This is not a game designed around collecting equipment, developing elaborate character builds, or repeatedly mastering difficult stages. Returning to it instead means approaching conversations differently and seeing how alternative decisions affect Audra's characterization and the direction of events. The presence of nine Steam achievements provides an additional incentive for completion-minded players, although the narrative remains the main attraction.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently Unknown, meaning the game does not have an official Steam Deck Verified or Playable classification. Its relatively modest technical requirements and straightforward style suggest it is not an especially demanding PC game, but an Unknown status should not be interpreted as guaranteed compatibility. Steam Deck players may need to experiment with controls or compatibility settings depending on their configuration.

Watch Me Jump is ultimately most successful when treated as a compact interactive drama that happens to take place within professional basketball rather than as a sports game. Its strongest qualities are its unusual premise, focused protagonist, dialogue-driven structure, and willingness to explore the personal cost of ambition. Its biggest limitation is equally clear: players wanting deep mechanics or actual basketball action will find relatively little of either.

As a narrative experiment, however, it has a distinctive identity. By transforming the pursuit of athletic greatness into a story about reputation, relationships, compromise, and personal values, it explores a side of professional sports that games rarely place at the center of the experience. Its limited scope will not appeal to everyone, but players who appreciate unconventional interactive storytelling should find a thoughtful and memorable drama here.

Rating: 8/10
